paragraphs.text: Computational sociology studies how social networks—like friendships, professional connections, or online communities—affect how people think and act. Instead of just drawing diagrams of who is connected to whom, researchers now look more closely at how frequent interactions shape behavior. If someone regularly chats with a group of friends who share strong opinions about climate change, they may gradually adopt similar views. These influences are especially strong when the conversations are emotionally charged or align with the person's values.
